```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Maggs_2026_fusidicAcid"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkag293> (open access)
* Fusidic acid model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Maggs_2026_fusidicAcid"))$description`
* Rifampicin model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Maggs_2026_rifampicin"))$description`

Maggs et al. ran a prospective, open-label drug-drug interaction study of oral
fusidic acid (500 mg three times daily) and oral rifampicin (300 mg twice
daily) in ten adults with staphylococcal infection. Participants were
randomised to one "index" drug for the first 24 hours, after which the second
drug was added and the combination continued for the treatment course.
Concentrations were measured in capillary dried blood spots on Day 1, Day 2
and at steady state (Day 28 +/- 7). The authors fitted two separate NONMEM
models, and both are packaged here:

* `Maggs_2026_fusidicAcid`: one-compartment, first-order absorption. Apparent
  clearance falls to 24.4% of its starting value from 24 h after the first
  dose (autoinhibition) and is then multiplied by 2.33 from 7 days after the
  first dose (rifampicin-mediated induction).
* `Maggs_2026_rifampicin`: joint rifampicin / 25-desacetyl rifampicin model
  (ADVAN6). One compartment for each analyte, absorption lag, a small
  pre-systemic conversion to the metabolite, all systemic rifampicin
  clearance forming the metabolite, and a 39.2% reduction in metabolite
  clearance when fusidic acid is co-administered.

# Population

Ten participants (three women) with osteoarticular (axial skeleton, 4),
large-joint (4, including 2 prosthetic joint infections), endovascular (1) and
small-joint (1) staphylococcal infections were recruited at two Melbourne
hospitals between 2019 and 2022 (Results paragraph 1). Median (IQR) age was
59 (48-68) years and body mass index 31 (29-35) kg/m2; baseline creatinine 78
(63-89) umol/L, albumin 27 (21-35) g/L. Four participants started with
fusidic acid and six with rifampicin. 96 fusidic acid, 101 rifampicin and 96
25-desacetyl rifampicin concentrations were modelled. Body weight, which both
models use for allometric scaling, is not reported.

# Virtual cohort and dosing

Body weight is not reported, so every virtual participant weighs 70 kg, the
models' reference weight; the simulations below therefore show the random
effects and the time-dependent changes, not the cohort's size spread. The
three sampling windows of Table 1 are Day 1 (first dose), Day 2 (24-32 h) and
steady state (Day 28, 648 h after the first dose).

```{r dosing}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261025)

n_sub <- 200
t_ss <- 648 # Day 28, the steady-state sampling day
windows <- tibble::tibble(
  period = factor(c("Day 1", "Day 2", "Steady state (Day 28)"),
                  levels = c("Day 1", "Day 2", "Steady state (Day 28)")),
  start = c(0, 24, t_ss)
)
grid_fa <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 8, by = 0.25), 0.583)))
obs_fa <- sort(unique(as.vector(outer(grid_fa, windows$start, "+"))))

# Fusidic acid 500 mg every 8 h from time 0 (the first fusidic acid dose).
make_fa_events <- function(n) {
  dose_times <- seq(0, t_ss, by = 8)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n), time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 500, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(n), time = obs_fa) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(WT = 70, T_FIRSTDOSE = time)
}
ev_fa <- make_fa_events(n_sub)
```

# Fusidic acid

## Time-dependent clearance

The two step factors on fusidic acid clearance are what the paper's
interaction finding rests on, so they are checked first. At steady state
AUCtau = Dose / (CL/F), so each phase's AUCtau ratio to Day 1 is the inverse
of its clearance factor. The paper reports a 4.09-fold rise by Day 2 and a
1.76-fold rise at steady state (Results); the packaged parameters give:

```{r fa-cl-ratio}
mod_fa <- readModelDb("Maggs_2026_fusidicAcid")
ini_fa <- rxode2::rxode(mod_fa)$theta
f_inh <- 1 + ini_fa[["e_autoinh_cl"]]
f_ind <- 1 + ini_fa[["e_rif_ind_cl"]]
ratio_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Phase = c("Day 2 (autoinhibition only)", "Steady state (both factors)"),
  `CL/F factor` = c(f_inh, f_inh * f_ind),
  `Model AUCtau ratio` = 1 / c(f_inh, f_inh * f_ind),
  `Paper AUCtau ratio` = c(4.09, 1.76)
)
knitr::kable(ratio_tab, digits = 3,
             caption = "AUCtau ratio relative to Day 1 (Maggs 2026 Results).")
```

The same ratio is reproduced by simulation. A typical 70 kg participant is
dosed to steady state three times with `T_FIRSTDOSE` held at a value inside
each phase, and PKNCA computes AUCtau over the last interval:

```{r fa-ss-auc}
mod_fa_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_fa)
phase_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  phase = c("Day 1", "Day 2", "Steady state"),
  T_FIRSTDOSE = c(0, 48, 400)
)
ev_phase <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(phase_tbl)), function(i) {
  d <- tibble::tibble(id = i, time = seq(0, 240, by = 8), evid = 1L,
                      amt = 500, cmt = "depot")
  o <- tibble::tibble(id = i, time = seq(232, 240, by = 0.1), evid = 0L,
                      amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(d, o) |> mutate(WT = 70, T_FIRSTDOSE = phase_tbl$T_FIRSTDOSE[i])
}) |> bind_rows() |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_phase <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_fa_typ, ev_phase, returnType = "data.frame")
conc_phase <- sim_phase |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc) |>
  left_join(phase_tbl |> mutate(id = row_number()), by = "id")
dose_phase <- ev_phase |> filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt) |>
  left_join(phase_tbl |> mutate(id = row_number()), by = "id")
nca_phase <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_phase, Cc ~ time | phase + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_phase, amt ~ time | phase + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 232, end = 240, auclast = TRUE)
))
auc_phase <- as.data.frame(nca_phase$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(phase, AUCtau = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(`Ratio to Day 1` = AUCtau / AUCtau[phase == "Day 1"])
knitr::kable(auc_phase, digits = 3,
             caption = "Typical-value steady-state AUCtau (mg*h/L) in each clearance phase.")
stopifnot(
  abs(auc_phase$`Ratio to Day 1`[auc_phase$phase == "Day 2"] / 4.09 - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(auc_phase$`Ratio to Day 1`[auc_phase$phase == "Steady state"] / 1.76 - 1) < 0.01
)
```

## Concentration-time profiles

```{r fa-sim}
sim_fa <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_fa, ev_fa, returnType = "data.frame")
sim_fa_win <- sim_fa |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(window = findInterval(time, windows$start)) |>
  mutate(period = windows$period[window],
         tsld = time - windows$start[window]) |>
  filter(tsld <= 8)
```

```{r fa-profile, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.5}
sim_fa_win |>
  group_by(period, tsld) |>
  summarise(q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), q50 = median(Cc), q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tsld, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~period) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time since last dose (h)", y = "Fusidic acid (mg/L)",
       caption = "Median and 90% prediction interval. Compare Figure 1, top row, of Maggs 2026.")
```

## NCA against the reported Cmax

The paper reports the mean raw observed fusidic acid Cmax from the protocol
samples (30-40 min, 1.5-2 h, 3.5-4.5 h and, on Days 1 and 2, 7-8 h):
8.68 mg/L on Day 1, 11.97 mg/L on Day 2 and 21.15 mg/L at Weeks 3-4 (Results
paragraph 4). These are study-day summaries, not dose-number summaries.
Figure 1 shows that only the four fusidic-acid-index participants had
fusidic acid on Day 1, and that for the six rifampicin-index participants
the Day-2 profile is their **first** fusidic acid dose. The simulated
comparison follows the same mix: 40% of the virtual participants are
fusidic-acid-index (Day 1 = first dose, Day 2 = 24-32 h) and 60% are
rifampicin-index (Day 2 = their first fusidic acid dose); all contribute at
steady state. Cmax is computed with PKNCA from the simulated observations
(`sim`, including residual error) at the protocol times and averaged across
participants to match the paper's arithmetic mean; the median and the
5th-95th percentiles are shown beside the observed range.

```{r fa-nca}
protocol_tsld <- c(0, 0.583, 1.75, 4, 7.5)
conc_fa <- sim_fa_win |>
  filter(abs(outer(tsld, protocol_tsld, "-")) |> apply(1, min) < 1e-6) |>
  filter(!(period == "Steady state (Day 28)" & tsld > 4.5)) |>
  mutate(time_rel = tsld) |>
  select(id, period, time_rel, Cc = sim)
dose_fa <- conc_fa |> distinct(id, period) |> mutate(time_rel = 0, amt = 500)
nca_fa <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_fa, Cc ~ time_rel | period + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_fa, amt ~ time_rel | period + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 8, cmax = TRUE)
))
cmax_id <- as.data.frame(nca_fa$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax") |>
  mutate(period = as.character(period)) |>
  select(id, period, cmax = PPORRES)
# Study-day view: ids 1-80 are fusidic-acid-index, 81-200 rifampicin-index.
# A rifampicin-index participant's Day-2 profile is a first fusidic acid dose,
# which in this time-since-first-fusidic-acid-dose simulation is the Day 1
# window.
cmax_study <- bind_rows(
  cmax_id |> filter(id <= 0.4 * n_sub, period != "Steady state (Day 28)"),
  cmax_id |> filter(id > 0.4 * n_sub, period == "Day 1") |>
    mutate(period = "Day 2"),
  cmax_id |> filter(period == "Steady state (Day 28)")
)
sim_cmax <- cmax_study |>
  group_by(period) |>
  summarise(cmax = mean(cmax), .groups = "drop")
published_fa <- tibble::tibble(
  period = c("Day 1", "Day 2", "Steady state (Day 28)"),
  cmax = c(8.68, 11.97, 21.15)
)
cmp_fa <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_cmax,
  reference = published_fa,
  by = "period",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_fa, caption = paste(
  "Mean Cmax by study day from protocol-time samples: simulated (70 kg,",
  "study arm mix) vs Maggs 2026 Results (n = 4, 10 and 9 evaluable).",
  "* differs by more than 20%."
))

cmax_study |>
  group_by(period) |>
  summarise(
    "Simulated median (mg/L)" = sprintf("%.1f", median(cmax)),
    "Simulated 5th-95th percentile (mg/L)" = sprintf(
      "%.1f-%.1f", quantile(cmax, 0.05), quantile(cmax, 0.95)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate("Observed range (mg/L)" = c("3.26-13.90", "4.15-30.0", "1.23-42.0")) |>
  dplyr::rename(Period = period) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Spread of the study-day Cmax (observed range from Maggs 2026 Results).")
```

Day 1 and Day 2 agree within 20% once the study's arm mix is respected; the
Day-2 rise is the autoinhibition step. At steady state the simulated mean is
about twice the observed mean, although the simulated median (about 26 mg/L)
is close to it and the observed range lies inside the simulated 5th-95th
percentile interval. Three features of the comparison push the simulated
steady-state mean up, and none of them points to a transcription error. The
observed mean comes from nine evaluable participants whose Cmax spans a
34-fold range. A proportional residual error of 72% on log-transformed data,
together with 78% inter-individual variability on CL/F, gives the simulated
maximum a long right tail that the arithmetic mean picks up (the residual
error's lognormal mean factor alone is `exp(0.722^2 / 2) = 1.30`). And the
virtual participants all weigh 70 kg, whereas the cohort's median BMI of 31
kg/m2 suggests heavier participants with allometrically larger clearance and
volume. The paper itself notes that "substantial variability was observed at
steady state" in its VPC (Figure 3) and reports a 95% CI of 0.049-34.9 for
the steady-state AUC ratio. The parameters are reproduced as published and
were not tuned to this target; the time-dependent clearance factors that
carry the paper's interaction finding are reproduced exactly above.

# Rifampicin and 25-desacetyl rifampicin

Two arms are simulated, each starting rifampicin 300 mg every 12 h at time 0:
the rifampicin-index arm adds fusidic acid at 24 h (`CONMED_FUSIDIC` switches
from 0 to 1), and the fusidic-acid-index arm takes fusidic acid throughout
(`CONMED_FUSIDIC = 1`). The occasion column follows the paper's four
sampling blocks.

```{r rif-events}
mod_rif <- readModelDb("Maggs_2026_rifampicin")
n_arm <- 100
grid_rif <- seq(0, 12, by = 0.25)
obs_rif <- sort(unique(as.vector(outer(grid_rif, windows$start, "+"))))
make_rif_events <- function(n, arm, id_offset) {
  dose_times <- seq(0, t_ss, by = 12)
  rif_index <- arm == "Rifampicin index"
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = id_offset + seq_len(n), time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 300, cmt = "depot")
  # Two error-model endpoints: observation rows name the parent state and
  # carry dvid = 1; rxode2 still returns both Cc and Cc_desacetylrif.
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = id_offset + seq_len(n), time = obs_rif) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(
      arm = arm,
      WT = 70,
      CONMED_FUSIDIC = if (rif_index) as.integer(time >= 24) else 1L,
      OCC = case_when(time < 24 ~ 1L, time < 168 ~ 2L, time < 648 ~ 3L, TRUE ~ 4L)
    )
}
ev_rif <- bind_rows(
  make_rif_events(n_arm, "Rifampicin index", 0),
  make_rif_events(n_arm, "Fusidic acid index", n_arm)
)
sim_rif <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_rif, ev_rif, returnType = "data.frame",
                           keep = c("arm", "CONMED_FUSIDIC"))
sim_rif_win <- sim_rif |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(window = findInterval(time, windows$start)) |>
  mutate(period = windows$period[window],
         tsld = time - windows$start[window]) |>
  filter(tsld <= 12)
```

```{r rif-profile, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
sim_rif_win |>
  select(arm, period, tsld, Rifampicin = Cc, `25-desacetyl rifampicin` = Cc_desacetylrif) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Rifampicin, `25-desacetyl rifampicin`), names_to = "analyte",
               values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(arm, period, analyte, tsld) |>
  summarise(q50 = median(conc), q05 = quantile(conc, 0.05),
            q95 = quantile(conc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tsld, q50, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ period, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time since last dose (h)", y = "Concentration (mg/L)",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       caption = "Median and 90% prediction interval. Compare Figure 1, middle and bottom rows, of Maggs 2026.") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## NCA by arm and period

```{r rif-nca}
conc_rif <- sim_rif_win |>
  mutate(time_rel = tsld) |>
  select(id, arm, period, time_rel, Cc, Cc_desacetylrif)
dose_rif <- conc_rif |> distinct(id, arm, period) |> mutate(time_rel = 0, amt = 300)
nca_one <- function(conc_col) {
  d <- conc_rif |> rename(conc = all_of(conc_col)) |> filter(!is.na(conc))
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(d, conc ~ time_rel | arm + period + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_rif, amt ~ time_rel | arm + period + id),
    intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 12, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                           auclast = TRUE)
  ))
  as.data.frame(res$result) |> mutate(analyte = conc_col)
}
nca_rif <- bind_rows(nca_one("Cc"), nca_one("Cc_desacetylrif"))
nca_rif_summary <- nca_rif |>
  group_by(analyte, arm, period, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
nca_rif_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Analyte = analyte, Arm = arm, Period = period,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "AUC0-12 (mg*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median simulated NCA over the 12-h dosing interval.")
```

The paper reports no rifampicin NCA values. Two in-model checks stand in for
a comparison:

* All systemic rifampicin is converted to the metabolite, so at steady state
  the metabolite-to-parent AUCtau ratio is
  `CL / (CLM x (1 - 0.392))` plus the small first-pass contribution, and the
  fusidic acid effect raises the metabolite's steady-state AUCtau by
  `1 / (1 - 0.392) = 1.64`-fold at unchanged rifampicin exposure.

```{r rif-check}
mod_rif_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_rif)
ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(id = 1:2, time = 0) |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(dt = seq(0, 240, by = 12)) |>
    mutate(time = dt, evid = 1L, amt = 300, cmt = "depot") |> select(-dt),
  tibble::tibble(id = 1:2) |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(228, 240, by = 0.05)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  mutate(WT = 70, OCC = 0L, CONMED_FUSIDIC = as.integer(id == 2))
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_rif_typ, ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame")
auc_typ <- sim_typ |>
  filter(time >= 228) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(
    auc_rif = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    auc_m = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc_desacetylrif, -1) + tail(Cc_desacetylrif, -1)) / 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
th <- rxode2::rxode(mod_rif)$theta
expected_m_ratio <- 1 / (1 + th[["e_conmed_fusidic_cl_desacetylrif"]])
check_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("Rifampicin AUCtau, without / with fusidic acid",
               "Metabolite AUCtau, with / without fusidic acid",
               "Rifampicin AUCtau vs F*Dose/CL (70 kg)"),
  Simulated = c(auc_typ$auc_rif[1] / auc_typ$auc_rif[2],
                auc_typ$auc_m[2] / auc_typ$auc_m[1],
                auc_typ$auc_rif[1] / (300 * (1 - th[["fm_desacetylrif"]]) / exp(th[["lcl"]]))),
  Expected = c(1, expected_m_ratio, 1)
)
knitr::kable(check_tab, digits = 3,
             caption = "Typical-value steady-state checks of the rifampicin model.")
stopifnot(all(abs(check_tab$Simulated / check_tab$Expected - 1) < 0.01))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Body weight.** Not reported; every virtual participant weighs 70 kg, the
  models' reference weight.
* **Time origin of the fusidic acid step factors.** Table 2 places the
  autoinhibition "after 24 hours from the first dose" and the rifampicin
  induction "after 7 days from the first dose". The packaged model reads both
  from `T_FIRSTDOSE`, the time since the first **fusidic acid** dose. The
  paper does not say whether its clock started at the first fusidic acid dose
  or at the first study dose (rifampicin, 24 h earlier, for six of ten
  participants). Figure 1 supports the fusidic-acid clock: the
  rifampicin-index participants' Day-2 fusidic acid profiles, their first
  fusidic acid dose 24 h after the first study dose, are mostly below 5 mg/L
  and lie under the fusidic-acid-index participants' Day-2 profiles, as
  expected if autoinhibition had not yet started. The induction
  step is time-based in the source and is not gated on rifampicin exposure;
  every participant was on rifampicin from the second study day.
* **Multiplicative combination of the step factors.** The paper prints both
  factors as `(1 + theta) x CL/F` without stating how they combine. The
  multiplicative form is the one that reproduces both reported AUCtau
  ratios exactly (4.09 and 1.76, above).
* **Supplementary run descriptions.** Table S1 describes the final fusidic
  acid run (1654) as an indicator "INDRA = 1 for Occasions 2 and 3" and Table
  S2 prints the metabolite interaction as `(1 - THETA(8) * (RF_only - 1))`
  without defining `RF_only`. The packaged models follow the main-text
  Tables 2 and 3 and the Results, which state the timing and direction of
  each effect explicitly.
* **First-pass parameter.** Table 3's `FP` = 0.981 is the fraction absorbed
  without first-pass metabolism; it is carried as its complement,
  `fm_desacetylrif = 0.019`, the fraction converted to the metabolite before
  reaching the circulation (the Results: "First-pass metabolism was <2%").
  The paper does not state the structure in equations; the packaged form
  splits the first-order absorption flux between the two compartments.
* **Molecular weight.** The paper assumes "all rifampicin is converted to
  25-desacetyl rifampicin" and does not mention a molecular-weight
  correction; amounts are carried in rifampicin mass units, so the
  metabolite's apparent volume and clearance absorb the 0.95 mass ratio.
* **Inter-occasion variability.** The four occasions are the paper's
  sampling blocks (Day 1, Day 2, Days 7-21, Day 28); occasions 2-4 share the
  occasion-1 variance. `OCC = 0` switches it off.
* **Absorption lag.** Table 3 prints an RSE of 0% for ALAG but a bootstrap
  95% CI of 0.487-0.582 h, so it is carried as estimated, not fixed.
* **Residual error.** Concentrations were log-transformed and the residual
  variability is reported as a proportional error; it is encoded as
  `prop()`, the linear-scale equivalent of an additive error on log
  concentrations.
* **Text inconsistency.** The Results quote "IIV on Ka and CL/F ... 110% and
  78%" for the rifampicin model, but Table 3 has no IIV on rifampicin CL/F
  and gives 30% on metabolite CLM/F; 77.8% is the fusidic acid CL/F value of
  Table 2. Table 3 is followed.
* **Matrix.** Concentrations are dried-blood-spot (whole blood) values, as
  in the source.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found for this article in Europe PMC on
  2026-11-17.
